newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.05 pct in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.05 pct in volatile trade.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.05 percent to close at 1.0760 per dollar in volatile trade on the commercial foreign exchange market due to a low supply of dollars, dealers said.

Some banks bought dollars early on Friday, anticipating continued dollar outlfows, which caused the local currency to drop 0.16 percent to 1.0782 per dollar, dealers said. On Thursday, forex contracts posted a $395.8 million deficit.

The real continued to trade between 1.0774 amd 1.0780 per dollar throughout the morning. But preliminary figures indicated that the dollar flows did not post a net deficit, which allowed the real to recover in the afternoon, dealers added.
At 1645 local/1945 GMT, preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $45 million surplus.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0801 per dollar, down 0.07 percent.
In the parallel market, the real fell 0.18 percent to end at 1.140 per dollar, traders said.
